solidViolations.context: Route file mixes routing (lines 46-274), date parsing validation (lines 72-85), error handling (lines 121-128), AND use case instantiation (lines 33-43). Has ~275 lines handling multiple responsibilities.

Route file (~493 lines) mixes: inline schema definitions (lines 24-135), 12 use case instantiations (lines 138-149), routing, validation, and error handling. Violates SRP by combining schema definition with routing logic.
Combines product AND category routes in one file. Instantiates 9 use cases (lines 30-39). Handles both entities in 235 lines with no clear separation.
Function directly accepts FastifyRequest/FastifyReply types from API layer. Mixes HTTP concerns (request parsing) with business logic (report aggregation). Should be a use case class receiving DTOs.
Order status transitions are hardcoded in private map (lines 9-18). Adding new status requires modifying this class. Should use configuration or strategy pattern.
Line 5: imports reportRepository directly from infrastructure container, bypassing repository interfaces. Depends on concrete implementation instead of abstraction.
Interface IProductRepository has 10 methods, including batchUpdateStock which is only needed by checkout/void use cases. Clients don't need all methods.

responsibilities: Inline JSON schema definitions for 8+ endpoints
godClasses.suggestion: Split into: schema file, use case factory, and separate route modules per resource (overview, alerts, history, opname)
Extract date parsing to middleware, use case factory pattern, response helper
Extract plugins to separate modules, health checks to dedicated file, use factory functions
Extract stock management to domain service, payment calculation to value object

files: All repository files (tenantId parameter in every method)

layerViolations.violation: Application layer imports infrastructure directly: imports reportRepository from '../../infrastructure/database/repositories/container.js'. Should depend only on domain interfaces.
API layer imports infrastructure: 'import { auditLogRepository } from "../../infrastructure/database/repositories/container.js"' at line 87. Middleware should not know about infrastructure details.
Application layer contains business logic about stock management. Stock operations (batchUpdateStock, stockLog creation) should be in domain service or infrastructure layer with domain events.
Entities are plain TypeScript interfaces with no behavior. This is anemic domain model - business logic scattered in use cases. Consider rich domain objects for complex entities like Order.
BaseRepository uses dynamic import 'protected db = () => import(...).then(m => m.getDb())'. This lazy loading pattern leaks infrastructure concerns and makes testing difficult.
Application layer accesses config directly: 'import { config } from "../../shared/config/index.js"' at line 9. TAX_RATE should be injected or come from domain.
All route files directly instantiate use cases: 'new CreateOrderUseCase(...)' at line 33 of order.routes.ts. This violates DI principle - use cases should be provided via constructor or factory.

featureEnvy.description: Routes access request.tenantId!, request.userId! directly. Should use TenantContext abstraction.
CheckoutUseCase manually builds stockUpdates array and calls batchUpdateStock. This logic (productId + quantity calculation) could be extracted to domain.
